questionText: A student needs to enroll for a minimum of 60 credits and at most 70 credits. The credits are divided among a project and three distinct sets of courses: core courses, specialization courses, and elective courses. A student must enroll for exactly 15 credits of core courses and exactly 20 credits of project. Additionally, a student must enroll for at least 10 credits of specialization courses. The maximum credits of elective courses that a student can enroll for is ________.
explanation:
Step 1: Set up the equation and constraints
Let total credits be $T = \text{Core} + \text{Project} + \text{Specialization} + \text{Elective}$.
Given constraints:
• Total credits: $60 \le T \le 70$
• Core courses = $15$
• Project = $20$
• Specialization courses $\ge 10$

Step 2: Formulate expression for Elective credits
$$15 + 20 + \text{Specialization} + \text{Elective} \le 70$$
$$35 + \text{Specialization} + \text{Elective} \le 70$$
$$\text{Elective} \le 35 - \text{Specialization}$$

Step 3: Maximize Elective credits
To maximize $\text{Elective}$, we minimize $\text{Specialization}$ to its minimum allowed value of $10$ while taking the upper limit for total credits ($70$):
$$\text{Elective}_{\text{max}} = 35 - 10 = 25$$

Therefore, the maximum elective course credits possible is 25.
